messages:
sylvia: Anybody else seeing huge slowdowns drawing choropleth maps on /customers/map in the EU canary? Works fine locally but canary dashboards are painfully slow.
ryan: Yup. Noticed it around 21:12 — charts take ~1.2s to paint vs ~120ms yesterday. Main-thread spikes.
maggie: Profiler snapshot looks like a big hit from a chunk that parses `topojson-client`. Bundle size for that chunk is +120KB vs previous canary. Also seeing duplicate module ids in the telemetry import.
leo: Is that the telemetry-sidecar roll from earlier? @deploy-bot rolled telemetry-proxy -> canary at ~21:10
deploy-bot: deploy: telemetry-proxy v3.4.2 -> canary started at 2025-07-01T21:10:12Z; status: success
ryan: Flame trace (lightweight):
```
main thread
- parseChunk (telemetry-proxy.js:234)
- renderChoropleth (choropleth.js:89)
- drawPaths (map-layer.js:47)
- requestAnimationFrame callback
```
sylvia: Also noticing KV-prefetch thrash: multiple widgets request the same topojson concurrently, causing duplicate downloads and eviction churn. Prefetch hitrate dropped to ~18% on canary.
maggie: That matches a prefetch policy change we shipped — switched client prefetch to `eager` in the telemetry rollout. Concurrency + eager prefetch -> chunk duplication across isolates.
leo: Quick mitigation: set `x-prefetch-policy: conservative` on the canary route via routing override (nginx header). That avoids a full rollback and is just routing config.
ryan: Changing to conservative may increase cold start latency for some flows, and affects routing quotas. tradeoff: avoid sustained main-thread work vs a small latency bump for colds.
maggie: I ran a staging test with conservative prefetch — render dropped to ~150ms. I'll open a minimal PR to add a canary override. No code rebuild needed if we do header injection.
sylvia: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/7891 — adds canary prefetch override + reorders telemetry import to avoid duplicate chunk side-effects.
leo: We should also emit a specific telemetry metric for per-chunk parse time (`client.chunk.parse_ms`) since current telemetry only has total parse and not per-chunk.
maggie: Added metric to the PR (one-line) and a dashboard tile for chunk parse p50/p95. Will ship with the canary override.
ryan: If it stays bad we need a rollback plan. What's Plan A/B?
sylvia: Plan A: flip canary allocation to previous telemetry-proxy revision via routing policy (instant). Plan B: remove eager prefetch header entirely and roll client change. I'll flip A if user impact >10%.
deploy-bot: alert: canary error rate increased by 0.8% and frontend LCP p95 spiked; routing alert to #incidents
sylvia: Flipping canary to previous telemetry-proxy now. Monitoring metrics, will report back. :eyes:
